item.title: Bainimarama allowed to travel to NZ for wife’s urgent treatment

item.content:encoded:
Former Prime Minister Voreqe Bainimarama has been allowed to travel to New Zealand to accompany his wife, Mary Bainimarama, who requires urgent specialist medical treatment in Auckland. This follows an application by his counsel to vary his bail conditions, which was heard in Sigatoka on Monday. Delivering his ruling virtually today, Suva High Court Judge Justice Daniel Goundar lifted Bainimarama’s stop-departure order for six weeks, allowing him to travel to Auckland. However, Justice Goundar has ordered that Bainimarama must return to Fiji by December 3rd for his Health Tender trial involving former Attorney General Aiyaz Sayed-Khaiyum and former Minister for Health Dr Neil Sharma. Bainimarama is charged with one count of abuse of office. Sayed-Khaiyum is charged with one count of abuse of office and one count of obstructing the course of justice, while Dr Sharma faces two counts of abuse of office and two counts of breach of trust by a person employed in the public service. Under the varied bail conditions, Bainimarama is permitted to travel only to Auckland and must remain there for the duration of his stay to accompany his wife during her medical treatment. Before his departure, he must lodge with the High Court Registry and serve on the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions a copy of his passport's photo page, his travel itinerary, including flight details, and his residential address and contact number in Auckland. Justice Goundar also ordered that Bainimarama must not travel to any other country and is restricted to travelling between his place of residence, the hospital and the airport while in Auckland. He is also prohibited from applying for or obtaining any visa or travel documents for another country. Upon returning to Fiji, Bainimarama must surrender his passport to the High Court Registry within 48 hours and report to the Officer-in-Charge at Totogo Police Station within 24 hours. Justice Goundar warned that if Bainimarama fails to return to Fiji and surrender himself into custody as required, his bail may be revoked and a warrant may be issued for his arrest.

item.title: Lautoka resident raises alarm over growing youth gambling concerns
item.description: A Lautoka resident has raised concerns about the increasing number of youths engaging in gambling as schools approach the holiday period, warning that children as young as 10 to 12 years old are involved. Speaking to fijivillage News, the resident says he has witnessed youths gambling for money with coconut sellers, with the money sometimes allegedly being used to buy drugs.
item.content:encoded:
A Lautoka resident has raised concerns about the increasing number of youths engaging in gambling as schools approach the holiday period, warning that children as young as 10 to 12 years old are involved.

Speaking to fijivillage News, the resident says he has witnessed youths gambling for money with coconut sellers, with the money sometimes allegedly being used to buy drugs.

He says he has also seen students leaving home for school before hiding their school bags in drains and engaging in gambling instead.

The resident says some of the areas where these activities take place include near sweet stalls in the city, Field 40 near the Andhra Sangam School bus bay, and Rifle Range.

He acknowledges that Police conduct patrols in these areas but says the youths appear to know the patrol schedules and disperse when a Police vehicle approaches.

The resident says the situation is concerning as gambling sometimes leads to fights when disagreements arise, putting other members of the public at risk.

He is calling on the relevant authorities to urgently look into the matter, particularly with children involving themselves in these activities.

Meanwhile, Lautoka City Council says the issue of students skipping school and gambling is serious matter and they are currently looking into the matter.

Questions have been sent to, Police, and Ministry of Children.

item.title: Man dies after vehicle crashes into post in Nabua
item.description: A man in his 30s has died after the vehicle he was driving crashed into a post along Jerusalem Road in Nabua last night. Police say the man allegedly lost control of his vehicle before hitting the post.
item.content:encoded:
A man in his 30s has died after the vehicle he was driving crashed into a post along Jerusalem Road in Nabua last night.

Police say the man allegedly lost control of his vehicle before hitting the post.

He was rushed to the CWM where medical officials confirmed his death.

A post-mortem examination will be conducted to determine the cause of death.

The national road death toll now stands at 48, compared to 64 for the same period last year.

item.title: FSC debt and rising costs put pressure on Govt spending “ Gounder
item.description: Fijians could face reduced funding for essential services such as housing, hospitals and education as rising debt servicing costs and financial pressures at the Fiji Sugar Corporation, alongside Government exposure to other state-owned enterprises including Fiji Airways, put pressure on public finances. This has been highlighted by Permanent Secretary for Finance Shiri Gounder during a panel discu
item.content:encoded:
Fijians could face reduced funding for essential services such as housing, hospitals and education as rising debt servicing costs and financial pressures at the Fiji Sugar Corporation, alongside Government exposure to other state-owned enterprises including Fiji Airways, put pressure on public finances.

This has been highlighted by Permanent Secretary for Finance Shiri Gounder during a panel discussion after World Bank Group Senior Economist Tihomir Stucka questioned what a credible path for Fiji would be to stabilise and eventually reduce its public debt.

Gounder says FSC is facing an extremely serious financial situation, with the Government guaranteeing more than $300 million in its debt and recently meeting the corporation's structural cash flow deficit.

He warns that if FSC's financial situation continues to deteriorate, the full fiscal exposure from its debt could fall on the Government.

He says rising debt servicing costs are reducing the amount of taxpayer money available for essential services, including housing, hospitals and education, and could also limit the Government's ability to respond to a future crisis.

Insert: Gounder on possible next crisis 29th Oct

Gounder says Government expenditure has grown by almost 40 percent in recent years, with a significant increase in operating expenditure contributing to a structural fiscal deficit of 7 percent this year.

He warns that without changes to the current approach, the Government could struggle to finance its budget.

Gounder says the growing fiscal deficit is also contributing to pressure on the current account and balance of payments, with exports remaining stagnant while imports continue to rise.

He says the Government needs to control expenditure growth and redirect funding from low-impact areas towards more productive investments.

Gounder also calls for a review of the size of the public sector , better targeting of social spending and subsidies, and measures to improve tax compliance and government revenue.

He says growing the economy and supporting the private sector would be the least painful way to address the country's fiscal challenges.
